program_name: Environmental and Land Engineering (Italian: Corso di Laurea Magistrale in Ingegneria per l'ambiente e il territorio). NOTE ON NAMING: the University of Trento uses two English renderings of the same LM-35 programme. The short official name used in the course-site title, in the university's master's-degree catalogue and in the 2026/27 admission call is 'Environmental Engineering' (call heading: 'Public selection for admission to the Master's Degree in ENVIRONMENTAL ENGINEERING'), while the descriptive text on the same official pages calls it 'the Environmental and Land Engineering MSc' - a literal translation of 'Ingegneria per l'ambiente e il territorio'. Both names refer to one and the same programme (ESSE3/course code family 0341-series, DICAM). It must not be confused with the separate UniTrento master's programme 'Environmental Meteorology and Climate Physics'. [uncertain]
teaching_language: MIXED - officially 'English and Italian', BUT a fully English pathway exists and is explicitly guaranteed. This is case (3) 'English and Italian' in form, functioning as case (1) 'fully English' in practice if the student picks the right curriculum. Evidence: (a) the official course pages and the university master's catalogue list 'LANGUAGE: English Italian'; (b) the Programme Regulations (Regolamento didattico 2025, DR n. 788 of 28/07/2025) state 'LINGUA IN CUI SI TIENE IL CORSO: italiano e inglese' and 'Gli insegnamenti possono essere impartiti in lingua italiana o inglese' (courses may be delivered in Italian or English); (c) the binding 2026/27 admission call states 'Le lingue ufficiali del corso di studio sono l'inglese e l'italiano. E' possibile seguire un orientamento formativo interamente in lingua inglese' - English translation: 'The official languages of the course are English and Italian. It is possible to attend a study track entirely in English.' COURSE-LEVEL BREAKDOWN (from the official Manifesto degli studi 2025/2026): THE ENTIRE FIRST YEAR IS IN ENGLISH - the manifesto heading reads 'I ANNO - lingua inglese' and covers Structural and geotechnical design (12 ECTS), Numerical methods for the environment (9), Ecological planning (9), Hydrodynamics (12), Urban hydraulic infrastructures (6), Hydrological modeling (6) and either Geomatics and remote sensing or Environmental transport processes (6). IN THE SECOND YEAR THE LANGUAGE DEPENDS ON THE CURRICULUM, and the manifesto labels each one explicitly: Curriculum I 'Risorse idriche e protezione del territorio / Water Resources and Land Protection' is labelled 'lingua italiana e inglese' (Italian and English) and contains at least three compulsory Italian-taught courses - River Engineering / Ingegneria fluviale (12 ECTS, marked 'in lingua italiana'), Stability of natural slopes and earth constructions / Stabilita dei pendii (6 ECTS, marked 'in lingua italiana') and Hydraulic hazards in mountain areas / Protezione idraulica dei territori montani (6 ECTS, marked 'in lingua italiana'); Curriculum II 'Environmental Quality and Remediation Technologies' is labelled 'lingua inglese'; Curriculum III 'Environmental Sustainability and International Cooperation' is labelled 'lingua inglese'; Curriculum IV 'Modelling and Simulation of Environmental Systems' is labelled 'lingua inglese'. CONCLUSION: three of the four curricula (II, III and IV) are entirely English-taught and, combined with the fully English first year, allow the whole 120-ECTS degree to be completed in English. Only Curriculum I is genuinely mixed and would require Italian. One residual non-English element applies to everyone: students whose mother tongue is not Italian must demonstrate Italian at A1 level (3 ECTS, activity type F) before the degree is awarded - this is a language-proficiency credit, not a taught subject. SCOPE DECISION: this programme SHOULD be counted as an English-taught programme for a prospective international student, because an entirely English study track is officially offered and formally guaranteed in the admission call.
campus: Trento - Mesiano district. The programme is run by the Department of Civil, Environmental and Mechanical Engineering (DICAM), whose main building and student support desk are at via Mesiano 77, 38123 Trento (TN); the Mesiano University Library (BUM) serves the same campus. Teaching is fully in person - the non-EU admission page states 'Lessons take place only in person' and that students must be in Trento for the start of classes. There is no Rovereto or San Michele all'Adige component.
degree_class: LM-35 - Ingegneria per l'ambiente e il territorio (Environmental and Land Engineering). The 2026/27 admission call writes the class as 'Class LM-35 R' (the 'R' marks the renewed/reformed ministerial class introduced by the 2023 reform of degree classes). Duration 2 years, 120 ECTS, 12 exams in total. Current academic rules: ex D.M. 270/04, Ordinamento 2025, Regolamento 2025 (issued by Rectoral Decree no. 788 of 28 July 2025).
admission_type: TWO DIFFERENT REGIMES, depending on the applicant's category. (1) EUROPEAN AND EQUIVALENT CITIZENS - OPEN ACCESS (accesso libero, no numero programmato). The course pages state 'ACCESS: Free' and the university catalogue lists 'Number of places: Free'. The Italian admission page states 'Il corso e ad accesso libero per studenti con cittadinanza italiana o europea ed equiparati': there is no ranking and no cap on places, but every applicant must submit an online request for verification of the admission requirements (richiesta di valutazione dei requisiti) and pass that check; an oral interview (colloquio) is added in the cases listed under academic_requirements. (2) NON-EUROPEAN CITIZENS LIVING OUTSIDE ITALY - RESTRICTED ACCESS via a public selection call based on qualifications and, where needed, an interview. The 2026/27 call sets 45 places for this category, of which 30 are reserved for candidates selected under the EMJM EESIC project (the Erasmus Mundus Joint Master 'Engineering for Environmental Sustainability and International Cooperation', coordinated by UniTrento with Instituto Superior Tecnico Lisbon and Universitat Politecnica de Valencia), leaving 15 places open through the ordinary non-EU call - the course website states 'Seats available: 15 (limited number)'. NO TOLC AND NO SAT is used for this programme in either regime. Applicants are ranked on a 100-point scale and need at least 50/100 to be declared eligible.
application_deadline_eu: Academic year 2026/2027: the online admission-requirements evaluation request (richiesta di ammissione / valutazione dei requisiti) must be submitted BY 27 NOVEMBER 2026. The Italian admission page states 'Per iscriverti al corso devi presentare la richiesta di ammissione online entro il 27 novembre 2026', and adds that the request is compulsory even for current UniTrento students and graduates who already meet the requirements, and that the applicant must already have earned AT LEAST 150 ECTS to submit it. ENROLMENT DEADLINE for a.y. 2026/2027: 21 December 2026 (via Esse3, after the Student Support service confirms the outcome and sends instructions); after receiving the matriculation number the student must complete the 'yearly enrolment' within 7 days to activate university services. GRADUATION DEADLINE for this category: the bachelor's degree must be obtained by 31 October 2026 (this same 31 October 2026 deadline also applies to non-EU citizens graduating in Italy who hold a valid Italian study residence permit). If the English B2 requirement is missing, it can be made up through the CLA English test, whose last 2026 session is registration 5 October - 13 November, written exam 23 November 2026, oral 4 December 2026 - deliberately scheduled to fit before the enrolment deadline.
application_deadline_non_eu: Academic year 2026/2027: 4 MARCH 2026 at 12:00 noon CET - a single, strict application window with no second session. The EUR 30.00 application fee must also be paid by that same deadline; failure to pay leads to automatic exclusion. The call states 'Only after the closing of the call (March 4, 2026 at 12.00) will the selection and admission process begin.' Applicants using a temporary @guest.unitn.it username are advised to create it at least 48 hours before the deadline. SUBSEQUENT MILESTONES: bachelor's degree to be obtained by 30 June 2026 for non-Europeans graduating outside Italy (by 31 October 2026 for non-Europeans graduating in Italy with a valid study permit); confirmation of the place by paying a non-refundable EUR 100.00 enrolment confirmation fee within the deadline given with the ranking list; pre-enrolment on the Universitaly portal within 2 weeks of confirmation (mandatory to obtain the admission letter and the study visa); the Italian entry visa must be obtained no later than 31 October 2026, otherwise admission is forfeited; enrolment at UniTrento by the deadline communicated by the staff.
entry_exam_or_test: NO WRITTEN ENTRANCE EXAM, NO TOLC AND NO SAT. (A) EUROPEAN/EQUIVALENT CITIZENS: only a documentary verification of the curricular requirements by the Collegio/Commissione di Area Didattica. An ORAL INTERVIEW (colloquio di verifica della preparazione personale) is required if: the weighted average of the bachelor's exams is between 22.00/30 and 23.99/30; or the qualification belongs to a degree class other than the ones listed; or the qualification was obtained abroad and judged suitable. Candidates missing curricular credits may be told to acquire additional credits (crediti formativi aggiuntivi) first - these can be earned by enrolling in UniTrento's 'Single courses for master's degrees' and passing the corresponding exams before the registration deadline. (B) NON-EUROPEAN CITIZENS: selection by evaluation of qualifications by a Selection Committee of at least three DICAM teaching staff nominated by Rectoral Decree (the Committee may meet by video conference), with an interview in person or by video conference if the uploaded documents are not sufficient to evaluate the application, or to verify personal preparation for holders of non-standard or foreign degrees. SCORING out of 100 points: (a) coherence between previous studies and the objectives of the master's degree - max 25 points; (b) curriculum (marks and results in previous studies, any post-graduate courses, extra-academic activities) plus the statement of purpose - max 70 points; (c) English certifications above the minimum required level, or officially recognised Italian language certifications - max 5 points. Eligibility threshold 50/100; ties are broken in favour of the youngest candidate; the ranking list is published on the programme webpage. (C) ENGLISH LANGUAGE TEST: applicants who cannot certify English B2 may sit the test organised by the UniTrento University Language Centre (CLA) - written part in person in Trento, oral part online. 2026 sessions for master's admission: S1 registration 27 March-20 April, written 27 April, oral 8 May; S2 registration 20 April-15 May, written 25 May, oral 5 June; S3 registration 16 May-25 June, written 6 July, oral 17 July; S4 registration 26 June-21 August, written 2 September, oral 11 September; S5 registration 24 August-2 October, written 12 October, oral 23 October; S6 registration 5 October-13 November, written 23 November, oral 4 December.
academic_requirements: QUALIFICATION: a bachelor's degree of at least 3 years. Standard route - an Italian bachelor's degree in class L-7 'Civil and Environmental Engineering' (ex D.M. 270/04) or the corresponding class 8 (ex D.M. 509/99), or a qualification obtained abroad recognised as valid and equivalent. ALTERNATIVE ROUTE (degree in a different class, an old-system Italian diploma awarded before ECTS, or a foreign qualification): the candidate must have earned minimum credits in the following scientific-disciplinary sectors (SSD): at least 24 ECTS across MAT/03 Geometry, MAT/05 Mathematical Analysis, MAT/06 Probability and Statistics, MAT/07 Mathematical Physics, MAT/08 Numerical Analysis; at least 18 ECTS across CHIM/06 Organic Chemistry, CHIM/07 Chemical Foundations of Technologies, FIS/01 Experimental Physics, FIS/03 Physics of Matter, ING-IND/10 Thermal Engineering and Industrial Energy Systems, ING-IND/11 Building Physics and Building Energy Systems, ING-IND/22 Materials Science and Technology; at least 30 ECTS across ICAR/01 Hydraulics, ICAR/02 Hydraulic Structures, Maritime Engineering and Hydrology, ICAR/03 Sanitary and Environmental Engineering, ICAR/06 Surveying and Mapping, ICAR/07 Geotechnics; at least 12 ECTS across ICAR/08 Structural Mechanics and ICAR/09 Structural Engineering. A bachelor's degree in the Civil-Environmental Engineering field that does not match the above, or another foreign qualification, may still be accepted: eligibility is assessed by the Selection Committee (non-EU) or by the Collegio di Area Didattica (EU/equivalent) on the basis of the candidate's curriculum studiorum and of the equivalence between the exams taken, their credits and the SSD sectors. MINIMUM GRADE: a credit-weighted average of at least 22.00/30 (or equivalent) in the bachelor's exams. Graded application of this threshold: average of 24.00/30 or above - admitted to the selection process directly; average between 22.00/30 and 23.99/30 - the Committee decides whether personal preparation is adequate, in practice through the interview; average below 22.00/30 - not admitted (the Programme Regulations state that graduates under D.M. 270/2004 or D.M. 509/1999 with a weighted average below 22.00/30 are excluded from access). NOT YET GRADUATED: allowed. EU/equivalent applicants must have earned at least 150 ECTS to submit the requirements-evaluation request, and must graduate by 31 October 2026. Non-EU candidates living abroad may apply without holding the degree provided they graduate by 30 June 2026 (31 October 2026 if graduating in Italy with a valid Italian study residence permit); undergraduate candidates must list in the transcript also the examinations not yet passed. PLACES AND QUOTAS: EU and equivalent citizens - open access, no cap ('Number of places: Free'). Non-EU citizens living abroad - 45 places in total, of which 30 reserved for candidates selected under the EMJM EESIC Erasmus Mundus project, leaving 15 places available through the ordinary non-EU call. Vacant places arising from withdrawals are reassigned following the ranking order. FURTHER REQUIREMENT: 'adequate academic background and professional experiences' (art. 2.1.v of the call). MISSING CURRICULAR REQUIREMENTS: EU/equivalent candidates may make them up by enrolling in Single Courses for Master's Degrees and passing the corresponding exams by the registration deadline. CATEGORY RULE: in case of dual citizenship where one is from an EU country, the EU citizenship prevails and the candidate cannot apply through the non-EU call.
language_requirements: ENGLISH - B2 of the CEFR is mandatory for admission in both regimes; candidates who cannot document it are considered not eligible in the non-EU selection. Accepted proofs: (1) an internationally recognised English language certificate, not older than 5 years, from the list of certificates accepted by the UniTrento University Language Centre (CLA) at https://www.cla.unitn.it/en/node/780 (point 2) - the selection committee may also consider certificates outside that list and assess their eligibility; (2) having passed a B2-or-higher university English exam during the previous degree, provided all four language skills (reading, writing, speaking, listening) were tested; (3) a written statement issued by the university where the bachelor's or master's degree was obtained certifying that the degree was officially taught in English (graduates of Italian universities submit a self-declaration under D.P.R. 445/2000; UniTrento students and graduates do not have to upload anything); (4) a self-declaration in the online application of being a citizen of an English-speaking country; (5) for EU/equivalent applicants only, passing the English test organised by UniTrento at the CLA (written part in person in Trento, oral part online) - the requirement can be made up after applying, and the applicant then e-mails the Student Support service to complete enrolment. English above the required B2, or an officially recognised Italian language certificate, is worth up to 5 extra points in the non-EU ranking. ITALIAN - not required for admission if the student chooses an English-taught curriculum, but required in two specific situations. (a) ENTRY-LEVEL ITALIAN B2 IF CHOOSING THE MIXED CURRICULUM: the Programme Regulations state that students who are not native Italian speakers, or who did not complete a cycle of secondary studies in Italian, and who intend to choose a curriculum with compulsory teaching activities in Italian, must also have Italian at least at level B2. In practice this concerns Curriculum I 'Water Resources and Soil/Land Protection', the only curriculum with compulsory Italian-taught courses. (b) ITALIAN A1 AS A GRADUATION REQUIREMENT: the Programme Regulations state that for students whose mother tongue is not Italian, knowledge of Italian will be verified before the degree is awarded, and that the 3 ECTS for the Italian language test may be granted directly to students holding a suitable certificate recognised by the Department or by the CLA, or otherwise earned at the CLA under arrangements agreed with the Department; the Manifesto degli studi specifies the level as A1 CEFR ('International students are required to demonstrate an adequate level of competence of the Italian Language (Level A1 CEFR - 3 ECTS/CFU - type F)'). This is a low-level proficiency credit counted among the 'Other activities' (type F), not an academic subject taught in Italian, and it does not affect admission. [uncertain]
required_documents: NON-EU CITIZENS LIVING ABROAD (online application on the UniTrento Apply portal for Degree Courses in English, https://webapps.unitn.it/Apply/en/Web/GoHome/master/MEnvEn_nEU_26; login with an @unitn.it username or a temporary @guest.unitn.it username created in the system): (a) a copy of a valid PASSPORT with photo and personal data - only the pages relating to personal information; (b) a copy of the BACHELOR'S DEGREE CERTIFICATE if already awarded, or a certificate of enrolment including the expected graduation date if not yet graduated - full information on the grading scale is required, otherwise the application will not be considered (Italian graduates submit a self-declaration under D.P.R. 445/2000; UniTrento students/graduates do not upload it); (c) the TRANSCRIPT OF ACADEMIC RECORDS listing all courses, exams, marks and credits, and including the weighted average mark and the minimum-to-maximum range of marks - undergraduate candidates must also list exams not yet passed; (d) a CURRICULUM VITAE ET STUDIORUM in English, preferably in the Europass European format; (e) a STATEMENT OF PURPOSE in English briefly explaining the reasons for applying to this master's programme; (f) proof of ENGLISH PROFICIENCY at B2 as described under language requirements. An official translation into English (or Italian) is required for every document not originally issued in English or Italian. Illegible documents are not considered and incomplete or unsubmitted application forms are excluded. FEES: application fee EUR 30.00, payable by 4 March 2026 (non-payment causes automatic exclusion); enrolment confirmation fee EUR 100.00 after admission, non-refundable under any circumstances and not deducted from tuition fees. AFTER ADMISSION: pre-registration at the competent Italian diplomatic representation and on the Universitaly portal (mandatory to receive the UniTrento admission letter and the study visa), then the study visa itself. UniTrento reserves the right to request a CIMEA/ENIC-NARIC statement of verification and/or statement of comparability; verification of foreign degrees is carried out only after admission and pre-enrolment are complete. EUROPEAN AND EQUIVALENT CITIZENS (online requirements-evaluation request, submitted after earning at least 150 ECTS): applicants who are students or graduates of another university must attach a SELF-DECLARATION OF THE EXAMS TAKEN, indicating for each exam the scientific-disciplinary sector (SSD), the credits (CFU), the date it was taken and the final mark; plus documentation of English B2. The Student Support service replies by e-mail stating whether additional credits must be acquired and whether the personal-preparation interview is needed, and then sends the instructions to complete the enrolment request in Esse3 by 21 December 2026.

uncertainty_notes:
1) ACCESS LIMITATION AND METHOD: corsi.unitn.it, www.unitn.it and offertaformativa.unitn.it sit behind a WAF that returns HTTP 405 to WebFetch and to curl with any header set, and offertaformativa.unitn.it additionally returned HTTP 503 for the course-programme sub-page. Three routes were used instead: (a) Internet Archive snapshots fetched with the raw 'id_' prefix (course home 20260511114431, non-EU admission 20260419174040, EU admission 20260410145131, documents page 20260415134626); (b) a public text-extraction reader proxy, which successfully returned the live corsi.unitn.it and www.unitn.it HTML and the official PDFs as text; (c) targeted web search for corroboration. Raw PDF bytes could not be downloaded through any of three CORS proxies, so the PDFs were read as proxy-extracted text rather than with a local PDF parser. Every fact above was cross-checked against at least two of these routes wherever possible, and the key language statement was verified in BOTH the binding Italian bando and the English courtesy translation.
2) PROGRAMME NAME - TWO OFFICIAL ENGLISH RENDERINGS: the research brief and the ministerial class use 'Environmental and Land Engineering', which is the literal translation of 'Ingegneria per l'ambiente e il territorio' and is the wording used in the descriptive text on the UniTrento course page ('the Environmental and Land Engineering MSc'). However, the page title, the browser title, the university's master's-degree catalogue, the URL slug (environmental-engineering-master) and the 2026/27 admission call all use the shorter 'Environmental Engineering'. These are the same programme, but a search for either name alone will miss half the official sources, and 'Environmental Engineering' also collides with similarly named programmes at other Italian universities.
3) THE MIXED-LANGUAGE FLAG IN THE BRIEF IS CONFIRMED BUT DOES NOT DISQUALIFY THE PROGRAMME: the brief warned that the official list shows this as an Italian programme. That is half correct - UniTrento formally classifies it as 'English Italian', not as English-only, and the Programme Regulations allow any course to be taught in either language. But the binding admission call explicitly guarantees that an entirely English study track can be followed, the whole first year is labelled 'lingua inglese' in the Manifesto, three of the four second-year curricula are labelled 'lingua inglese', and UniTrento itself lists 'Environmental Engineering' among its 'Master's degrees in English' for the purposes of the non-EU tuition-fee scale and runs the non-EU admissions through its 'Degree Courses in English' application portal. The programme therefore qualifies as English-taught for a student who avoids Curriculum I.
4) THE ONE CURRICULUM TO AVOID: Curriculum I 'Water Resources and Soil Protection' (called 'Risorse idriche e protezione del territorio / Water Resources and Land Protection' in the Manifesto - note the Soil/Land inconsistency between the course page and the Manifesto) is the mixed-language track and contains at least 24 ECTS of compulsory Italian-taught teaching. A non-Italian speaker choosing it would additionally need Italian at B2 for admission. The choice of curriculum is declared at enrolment and can be changed in later years.
5) ITALIAN A1 GRADUATION CREDIT - SCOPE NOT FULLY RESOLVED: the Programme Regulations state generally that Italian proficiency is verified for non-native speakers before the degree is awarded and that 3 ECTS are attached to it, which reads as applying to all students of the programme. In the Manifesto tables the matching footnote ('Level A1 CEFR - 3 ECTS/CFU - type F') is printed against the 'Altre attivita / Other Activities' row of one curriculum only (Modelling and Simulation of Environmental Systems) rather than against all four. Because the PDF had to be read through a text-extraction proxy that flattens the table layout, it could not be established with certainty whether the footnote is meant to apply to that curriculum alone or to every curriculum. The safe reading, consistent with the Regulations, is that it applies to all international students. Either way it is an A1-level proficiency credit, not an Italian-taught subject.
6) NON-EU PLACES - THE 45 vs 15 DISCREPANCY IS REAL AND EXPLAINED: the admission call says 45 places, the course website says 15. Both are correct: 45 is the total non-EU allocation, 30 of which are ring-fenced for students selected through the EMJM EESIC Erasmus Mundus Joint Master (a separate application procedure run by the EESIC consortium of UniTrento, Instituto Superior Tecnico Lisbon and Universitat Politecnica de Valencia, with its own calendar, its own EUR 8,000/year fee for non-scholarship students and its own Erasmus Mundus scholarships of EUR 1,400/month). Only the remaining 15 are contestable through the ordinary UniTrento non-EU call described here. Applicants interested in the EESIC route must apply separately at projects.unitn.it/eesic - that procedure was not researched in detail and its deadlines differ.
7) DEADLINE ASYMMETRY IS EXTREME: non-EU applicants must apply by 4 March 2026 in a single window with no second session, while EU/equivalent applicants have until 27 November 2026. A non-EU candidate who misses 4 March 2026 has no fallback for 2026/2027 through this call. The 27 November 2026 EU date was found only on the Italian-language admission page (the English page carries the notice 'The content of this page is available in Italian only'), so it has no official English-language statement; it is nonetheless the same university-wide November deadline that recurs across UniTrento master's programmes.
8) EU FEES NOT DETAILED: the score-based fee scale (up to EUR 6,000/year, reduced or waived by admission score) applies to non-EU citizens living abroad. EU and equivalent students instead pay UniTrento's ordinary income-related (ISEE-based) contribution, whose brackets were not retrieved for this programme; the general fees hub is linked in tuition_or_fees_link. The exact number of scholarships reserved for non-EU students in 2026/27 is not published in advance - the call states it is disclosed only when the ranking is published.
9) SECOND-YEAR CURRICULA ARE NEW: the Manifesto heading reads 'II ANNO - CURRICULA attivi dal 2026/27', i.e. the four curricula in their current form become active in the second year from 2026/27 under Ordinamento/Regolamento 2025, while the parallel 2025/26 second-year Manifesto still runs the previous Regolamento 2024 structure and marks its first year as 'disattivato'. The curriculum content and the language labelling are identical between the two documents, but the offering could still be adjusted for 2026/27 and no 2026/2027 Manifesto degli studi had been published at the time of research - the documents page still listed only the 2025/2026 and earlier Manifestos.
10) NOT VERIFIED: the ranking-list publication date for the non-EU 2026/27 selection (the call says only that it is published on the programme webpage after the evaluation); the exact deadlines for confirming the place and for enrolling, which are communicated individually with the ranking; whether the CLA English test is available to non-EU applicants living abroad (the call lists it only among the EU/equivalent make-up routes, and the written part must be sat in person in Trento); and the per-course language of the free-choice (TAF D) electives listed in Table 1 of the Manifesto, although all of those are titled in English and several are shared with the English-taught Environmental Meteorology and Energy Engineering masters.
